metadata.note: The Wichita Valley Lines: five Colorado & Southern-controlled Texas companies operated as one by the Wichita Valley Railway (the operating company from 1906/1908 to the 13 Jun 1952 merger into the Fort Worth and Denver City). Drawn: the Wichita Falls - Seymour - Stamford - Anson - Abilene through route, Wichita Falls - Seymour 1890-1949 and Seymour - Stamford - Abilene 1907-1949, ending with the last passenger train on 29 Oct 1949. Stamford - Abilene is two features because the trains changed track: the Abilene & Northern's own Anson - Abilene line 1907-1910, the Abilene & Southern's under lease from 1 Oct 1910. One company, one colour throughout (Rule 4): the WV Railway ran every drawn year; the FW&D merger post-dates passenger service.
metadata.company_colour: #918B30 picked programmatically: used by no company in data/, the largest Lab distance to any existing colour among the candidates tried, and far from the FW&D's #8E1B3C (the FW&D did not run these trains before 1952).
sources: research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt (Feb 1952 Official Guide index: Wichita Valley stations daggered "For freight only", Table 79)
not_yet_sourced: Operator 1942-1949 (report U1): wichitavalleynrhs.org says the Wichita Valley Lines 'operated independently until the Fall of 1942'; what happened then is not stated. A Fort Worth Star-Telegram photo of 1 Dec 1940 (UTA Special Collections, https://mavmatrix.uta.edu/specialcollections_startelegram1940s/4952) records the Colorado and Southern's application to lease the FW&DC and Wichita Valley properties, hearing 2 Dec 1940, outcome not found. If the FW&D (or the C&S) took over operation in 1942, every feature needs a split at 1942 with the later years in that company's colour (Rule 4). Drawn as Wichita Valley throughout until proven otherwise. The 1951 Guide still lists the WV as a separate company sharing FW&D officers - joint management, not proof of an operating contract.
Seymour - Stamford opening (U4): ICC says the WV operated 'the first section' from about 1 Nov 1906; when the whole line reached Stamford (1906, 1907 or 1908) is not sourced. Drawn from 1907.

Anson - Abilene alignment (U5): the A&S lease of 1 Oct 1910 ran 10 years; whether WV trains stayed on the A&S track 1921-1949 or returned to the A&N's own line is not sourced. Drawn on the A&S track 1911-1949.
Abilene - Stamford 1 Jan 1907 - 31 Jan 1908: A&N-owned under a C&S 'informal lease'; who ran the trains is not stated. Drawn as Wichita Valley.
1949 end (U7): both sources (wichitavalleynrhs.org, City of Wichita Falls timeline) are secondary; no newspaper or ICC discontinuance order seen.
headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates for every year: no Wichita Valley timetable has been read (Table 79 of the Feb 1952 Guide is unreadable in the OCR).

Wichita Falls - Holliday - Mabelle alignment: the 1890 route out of Wichita Falls is not located (the trace uses a later-looking connection via the FW&D main and an industrial spur, 1.5 mi longer than Fowler's mileposts), and Holliday - Mabelle (28 mi) is drawn as straight legs between hamlet points.

Cross-report conflict: research/branches/colorado_and_southern_railway.txt block [72] says WV passenger service ran 'after 1951'; this layer follows the WV report (Table 78 'Freight Service only', stations daggered, last train 29 Oct 1949).
metadata.omitted: Report blocks [4]-[6], all 'drawable: NONE': [4] Stamford - Spur (ex-Stamford & Northwestern, 82.9 mi, opened 1909) - no passenger year confirmed; the 1 Nov 1909 opening train is not shown to have carried passengers, the Feb 1952 Guide prints its Table 78 'Freight Service only', and the 1967 closure is an end of freight, not of passengers. [5] Wichita Falls - Byers (ex-Wichita Falls & Oklahoma, 22.1 mi, 1904-1942) and [6] Byers - Waurika, OK (c.7.5 mi, 1923-1942) - no confirmable passenger year; Fowler lists the stations but without a date letter, and the 1942 abandonment is not a passenger end. Also omitted: all freight after 29 Oct 1949 (Rule 1).
metadata.freight_only_audit: Written passenger-only from the start: no freight-only segments or features; post-1949 freight and the undated Stamford - Spur and Wichita Falls - Byers - Waurika branches are omitted.

properties.speed_source: Estimate (Rule 3): no Wichita Valley timetable has been read, so neither the speed nor the frequency is sourced. 40 km/h is a typical figure for a West Texas branch-line local/motor car of the period.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py over railtrace half-degree tiles plus fetch_gap (OSM historic/trail ways and OpenHistoricalMap) and a probe of every old_railway_operator value in the corridor. No OSM way carries a Wichita Valley old_railway_operator (values present: MP, CB&Q, MKT, AT&SF, WF&S, Southwestern Railway, EWF&G); the grade is mapped as railway=razed ways NAMED 'Wichita Valley', which the trace treated as the company's own. Wichita Falls - Holliday: BNSF Red River Valley Subdivision (ex-FW&D main, 1060665543 etc.) west from the Wichita Falls depot area to an industrial spur (334820111, 476843269) running south to Allendale, then untagged railway=abandoned 1547977572/170831710 and the 'Wichita Valley Daylight Trail' rail-trail (cycleway 316599195) into Holliday. Mabelle - Seymour: razed 'Wichita Valley' way 156544555. OHM has no Wichita Valley ways (only the FW&D, MKT, WF&S, Southwestern and Gulf, Texas & Western). Waypoints: Nominatim hamlets Mankins, Dundee, Fulda, Mabelle (type checked: hamlet); Holliday and Seymour town boundaries; Wichita Falls hand-pinned to the FW&D depot area (the geocode is the city centroid).
properties.geometry_quality: Drawn 53.5 mi against a documented 51.5 mi (Fowler) / 52.0 mi (ICC 51.36 + 0.66). STRAIGHT-LINE LEGS, 28.1 mi in all: Holliday - Mankins 6.7 mi, Mankins - Dundee 6.7 mi, Dundee - Fulda 7.9 mi, Fulda - the east end of the surviving grade about 1 mi east of Mabelle 6.8 mi (Fowler: Holliday 14.3 -> Mabelle 42.3 = 28.0 mi). No OSM way (tagged or untagged, including a bare railway=abandoned check of the tiles), rail-trail or OHM way survives there, so the legs join the Nominatim hamlet points, which are only approximately on the old line. Traced: Wichita Falls - Holliday 16.3 mi against Fowler's 14.3 - about 2 mi long. Allendale falls at 9.2 mi on the trace against Fowler's 7.7, so the Wichita Falls end (west along the FW&D main, then south down a surviving industrial spur) is probably a LATER connection than the 1890 alignment, which is not located in OSM inside the city. Mabelle - Seymour 9.2 mi traced on the razed grade. Draws the alignment as abandoned (post-1949 freight era); no realignment is known on the surviving pieces.

segments.note: Wichita Valley Railway (inc. 8 Feb 1890), Wichita Falls - Maples - Allendale - Holliday - Mankins - Dundee - Fulda - Mabelle - Seymour, 51.36 mi built Apr - 1 Sep 1890 plus 0.66 mi at Seymour 1904 (ICC Valuation vol. 134; 51.989 mi owned; Fowler 51.5). START 1890: ICC - operated by its own organization 'from September 1, 1890'; TSHA reports passenger revenue of $13,483 for 1891, so passenger service existed by 1891 at the latest; the first passenger year is taken as the 1890 opening. Promoted by Grenville M. Dodge and Morgan Jones of the FW&DC. In the final years service was a motor car Wichita Falls - Abilene (Wikipedia FW&D). Operator: the Wichita Valley Railway, which operated all the Wichita Valley Lines - under lease from 1 Feb 1908 - until the 1952 FW&D merger. C&S control (14 Nov 1905) and Burlington's purchase of the C&S (Dec 1908) did not change who ran the trains (TSHA: 'continued to be operated separately'); USRA federal control 1918-1920 is noted only. Unresolved (see metadata.not_yet_sourced): whether the FW&D or the C&S took over operation in 1942. END 1949: last passenger train on the Wichita Valley, Wichita Falls - Abilene, 29 Oct 1949, a CB&Q-numbered doodlebug (motor car No. 9842) - wichitavalleynrhs.org, same date in the City of Wichita Falls timeline. Both are secondary; corroborated (not proved) by the Feb 1952 Official Guide index daggering the main-line stations freight-only for Sept 1951. Freight continued (FW&D from the 13 Jun 1952 merger, BN from 1970, Southern Switching Co. from 16 May 1994) and is not drawn (Rule 1). headway_min 1440 (one daily train each way) is an ESTIMATE - no timetable frequency has been sourced for any year.
sources: Segment-level: start from ICC Valuation Reports vol. 134 (Wichita Valley Ry: operated from 1 Sep 1890) and TSHA (1891 passenger revenue); end from wichitavalleynrhs.org (last train 29 Oct 1949), corroborated by the Feb 1952 Official Guide index. Headway not sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Wichita Valley Railroad (inc. 12 Oct 1905), Seymour - Fancher - Bomarton - Goree - Munday - Weinert - Josselet - Haskell - McConnell - Stamford, 60.881 mi (ICC vol. 134; Fowler 61.2). Operated by the Wichita Valley Railway from about 1 Nov 1906 (ICC: 'when the first section of its road was placed in operation' - how far is not stated), under formal lease from 1 Feb 1908. START 1907: the confirmed year - 1 Jan 1907 is when the Abilene & Northern opened Stamford - Abilene as the south end of the through Wichita Falls - Abilene route; Seymour - Haskell may have carried trains from Nov 1906 (Haskell depot built 1906, THC). The 1906 start is withheld, not denied. The Feb 1952 Guide index daggers Goree, Munday and Bomarton freight-only; Seymour and Haskell print without the dagger (almost certainly an OCR drop) - not evidence of 1951 service. Operator: the Wichita Valley Railway, which operated all the Wichita Valley Lines - under lease from 1 Feb 1908 - until the 1952 FW&D merger. properties.line: Wichita Valley: Stamford – Abilene (via A&N track)
properties.speed_source: Estimate (Rule 3): no Wichita Valley timetable has been read, so neither the speed nor the frequency is sourced. 40 km/h is a typical figure for a West Texas branch-line local/motor car of the period.
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py; the A&N and A&S grades were each traced with the opposite company's ways un-preferred so the router could not swap between the parallel lines. Stamford - Anson on razed/abandoned ways named 'Wichita Valley' (136144505, 166885163). Anson hand-pinned to the point where the A&N and A&S grades meet at the south edge of town (Fowler's Anson Junction, 0.8 mi south of Anson); Stamford hand-pinned to the junction of the Haskell and Anson grades; Hawley from Nominatim (town boundary, checked); Abilene town boundary centroid, 0.3-0.7 km from the line ends.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 37.8 mi against a documented 39 mi (TSHA) / 38.5 mi (Fowler 112.7 -> 151.2). No straight-line legs. Stamford - Anson 13.9 mi (Fowler 13.9); Anson - Abilene 23.9 mi on the A&N's OWN grade (OSM razed ways named 'Wichita Valley' 21696219 and 'Chicago Burlington and Quincy' 7850063/166800480, then the surviving CB&Q-named spur 166800486 into Abilene), which runs about 1 km east of the parallel Abilene & Southern grade. ERA: this feature is drawn only for 1907-1910, because from 1 Oct 1910 Wichita Valley trains used the Abilene & Southern's Anson - Abilene track under lease (ICC vol. 134) - see feature wv-stamford-abilene-via-as. Which of the two OSM grades is the A&N and which the A&S south of Anson is inferred from their names and their meeting the Stamford line, not from a primary map.

segments.note: Abilene and Northern Railway (chartered 5 Feb 1906), Stamford - Penick - Anson - Hawley - Lanius - Abilene, 39 mi, 'open for service on January 1, 1907' (TSHA; ttarchive 'officially opening for business on January 1, 1907'). 1 Jan 1907 - 31 Jan 1908: A&N-owned, the C&S held all its stock and 'operated the line under an informal lease' (ttarchive) - who physically ran the trains in those 13 months is not stated, so no separate feature is drawn for them. From 1 Feb 1908 leased to and operated by the Wichita Valley Railway, 'operated under this arrangement until June 1952' (ttarchive). END 1910 on THIS alignment: from 1 Oct 1910 the Wichita Valley used 24.513 mi of the Abilene & Southern main line Anson - Abilene under a 10-year lease paid per train-mile (ICC vol. 134), so 1911 onward is drawn on the A&S alignment (feature wv-stamford-abilene-via-as); 1910 is drawn here because nine months of it ran over the A&N. This is a change of track, not an end of service. headway_min 1440 (one daily train each way) is an ESTIMATE - no timetable frequency has been sourced for any year.
sources: Segment-level: start from TSHA (Abilene and Northern) and ttarchive (opened 1 Jan 1907; WV lease 1 Feb 1908); the 1910 alignment change from ICC Valuation Reports vol. 134 (A&S lease from 1 Oct 1910). Headway not sourced (estimate).

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 37.2 mi. No straight-line legs. Stamford - Anson 13.9 mi on the Wichita Valley's own grade (same geometry as wv-stamford-abilene-via-an), then Anson - Abilene 23.3 mi on the ABILENE AND SOUTHERN grade: OSM 'Burlington Northern' abandoned way 166885164 (Anson - Hawley) and razed 'Abilene and Southern' way 166800484 (Hawley - Abilene) - against the ICC's 24.513 mi of A&S main line Anson - Abilene leased from 1 Oct 1910 and Fowler's Anson 126.6 -> Abilene 151.2 = 24.6 mi. This is a DIFFERENT alignment from the A&N's own Anson - Abilene line, which is drawn only for 1907-1910 (wv-stamford-abilene-via-an). Drawn for 1911-1949 on the A&S track throughout; the ICC lease was for 10 years and no source says whether Wichita Valley trains stayed on the A&S track after 1920 (see not_yet_sourced). Draws the alignment as abandoned.

segments.note: Wichita Valley through trains Stamford - Anson over the A&N's own track, then Anson Junction - Abilene Junction over the Abilene and Southern (a Texas & Pacific affiliate) under the lease of 1 Oct 1910 (ICC vol. 134: 24.513 mi, 10 years, paid per train-mile; Fowler shows 'Anson Junction' 127.4 and 'Abilene Junction (A&S)' 151). Drawn from 1911, the first full year on the A&S track. The Feb 1952 Guide index daggers Hawley freight-only.
